extracted.intended_audience: NIH reviewers and research scientists preparing an R01-style application on fungal pathogenesis / Histoplasma genetics
extracted.subtask_description: A research-plan section of an NIH-style grant proposing a forward-genetics screen to identify Histoplasma capsulatum virulence factors using T-DNA insertional mutagenesis and macrophage-based high-throughput assays. Includes Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Preliminary Data, and Approach details.

rubrics_metrics.name: T-DNA element selection (pBHt2) performance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a T-DNA element that provides high transformation efficiency and minimal vector backbone carryover, preserving the left- and right-border (LB/RB) T-DNA ends to enable rapid mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pBHt2 was chosen because it yields high transformation efficiency (79 ± 20 per 5x10^7 yeast), low frequency of vector backbone carryover (8%), and preserves LB and RB ends in 87% and 94% of integrations respectively. Mapping relies on intact LB/RB ends as anchors; avoid T-DNA constructs that frequently transfer backbone or truncate borders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomness of integration / absence of insertional hotspots
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that T-DNA integration is random across the genome with no insertional hotspots (defined here as multiple insertions within 5000 bp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random integration is essential for unbiased mutagenesis. Empirical mapping of 70 transformants found no evidence of hotspots. Note: integrations commonly occur in promoter regions (~36%) but promoter or intron insertions can still effectively disrupt gene function, expanding useful target space beyond coding sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping methodology and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hemi-specific PCR (e.g., thermal asymmetric interlaced PCR / TAIL-PCR) anchored in T-DNA ends to amplify and sequence genomic DNA flanking insertions, then identify disrupted loci by comparison to transcriptome-based gene models or de novo predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nested LB/RB-specific primers with random degenerate primers to amplify flanking sequence. Match proximal ends to the T-DNA to confirm anchor and map remaining sequence to the genome. Eliminate mutants that disrupt known virulence genes by targeted PCR prior to further analysis. Complementation should be used to confirm phenotype–mutation linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-throughput macrophage-based screen design criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the phenotypic assay to (1) measure only macrophage numbers in mixed macrophage/yeast populations, (2) be sensitive and quantitative to detect partial virulence defects, and (3) require minimal manipulations to permit high-throughput screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To meet these criteria the investigators engineered macrophages to constitutively express a lacZ transgene (P388D1-lacZ) assayed with a one-step lysis and chromogenic (ONPG) or fluorescent (FDG) substrate. Alternative reporter readouts (e.g., RFP-expressing yeast) permit non-destructive quantification of intracellular yeast. Avoid assays that require heavy manual processing like CFU recovery for high-throughput contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay statistical sensitivity / power
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish assay variability and statistical power to detect biologically relevant attenuation levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on assay variability with wild-type yeast, the LacZ assay sensitivity is sufficient to discriminate a 15% decreased rate of macrophage killing with 90% statistical power. Use such power calculations to set realistic selection thresholds and sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutant selection thresholds for attenuated virulence
rubrics_metrics.description: Define numeric cutoffs for selecting mutants as attenuated in the primary screen and/or follow-up assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims state selection of mutants that exhibit at least 50% reduction in intramacrophage growth and/or at least 50% decreased ability to lyse macrophages. In pilot screens a pragmatic cutoff of ≥30% attenuation was used to identify candidates that were reproducible in repeat assays; report the threshold used and justify it with power/variability data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library size and genomic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the number of independent mutants to generate and the resulting genome coverage to ensure adequate probability of hitting genes of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal plans generation of a 40,000-mutant library representing ~2.5-fold coverage of the Histoplasma genome. Choose library size to balance coverage goals with practical screening throughput and downstream mapping/validation capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen logistics and experimental format
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement workflows that permit arraying, storage, infection, and readout compatible with high-throughput processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Array individual transformants into 96-well plates for growth (48 h), infect P388D1-lacZ macrophages at MOI 1:1 in 96-well plates, and quantify macrophage survival (lacZ) or intracellular yeast (RFP) without destroying host cells. Use automated/plate-reader compatible substrates and minimize per-well manual steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification scheme for virulence defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify identified mutants according to the mechanistic basis of attenuation to guide prioritization for follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify mutants into: (1) deficient in macrophage entry, (2) impaired survival in macrophages, (3) normal survival but impaired replication in macrophages, and (4) normal replication but deficient ability to cause macrophage lysis. Use kinetic, non-destructive RFP readouts and macrophage-lysis assays to assign classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization criteria for candidate virulence factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize mutants/candidate genes for further characterization based on objective biological features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize by severity of virulence attenuation, conservation of the factor among intracellular pathogens, and increased expression in pathogenic- compared to non-pathogenic-phase cells. Use these axes to select diverse mechanistic classes and maximize translational relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter-strain equivalence validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that reporter strains (e.g., RFP-expressing yeast; lacZ macrophages) behave equivalently to wild-type in key metrics so reporter readouts reflect native biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm RFP-fluorescent Histoplasma has identical entry rate, intracellular survival, and growth within macrophages compared to wild-type yeasts. Use control infections and CFU-based validation as needed to establish reporter fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-of-principle and phenotype translation to in vivo
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide preliminary data showing that mutants identified by the screen (e.g., CBP1, HSP82 promoter insertions) produce the expected attenuated phenotypes and that these translate to in vivo models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that known virulence-factor disruptions (e.g., CBP1) are recovered by the screen and that at least some mutants (e.g., HSP82 promoter insertion) display reduced virulence in animal models. Use complementation to link phenotype to mutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility metrics for mapping success
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate empirically that mapping methods can recover insertion sites at scale and that T-DNA characteristics permit efficient mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mapping success (e.g., mapped >100 T-DNA insertions), frequencies of LB/RB preservation, and low backbone carryover. Use these metrics to justify capacity to map large numbers of mutants from the library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen yield / mutant isolation frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Document pilot screen hit-rate statistics to set expectations for full-scale screening and follow-up workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot data: screened 3478 mutants, identified 21 mutants with ≥30% reduced macrophage-lysis (maintained on repeat assays), giving an isolation frequency of 0.76% ± 0.30 (n=8). Use observed hit rates to estimate number of candidates from larger libraries and plan mapping/validation resources accordingly.
